prompt: A boutique hotel group wants to grow profit by 30%. The candidate's framework: (1) Raise room rates; (2) Increase occupancy; (3) Cut operating costs. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: higher rates lower occupancy
options.feedback: Rate and occupancy affect each other, but they are different drivers of room revenue, so they belong in separate buckets.

options.text: Missing: revenue beyond rooms, such as food, bar and events
options.feedback: Right. Room rates and occupancy only cover room revenue. Food, bar and events are a large part of a boutique hotel's profit and are missing.

options.text: Bucket 1 doesn't belong: boutique hotels have no room to raise rates
options.feedback: Nothing says rates are capped. Rate is usually a hotel's strongest profit lever.

options.text: It's a generic revenue tree: it doesn't reflect boutique hotels
options.feedback: Rate and occupancy are the right hotel drivers. The flaw is that only room revenue is covered.

explanation: Profit grows from room revenue (rate, occupancy), revenue beyond rooms (food, bar, events) and costs. Rate and occupancy only cover rooms. Opening new hotels is another lever worth adding.

extras.corrected_framework: Room revenue (rate, occupancy); revenue beyond rooms (food, bar, events); new properties; cost efficiency
